chunks: Al-Bazanti narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who struck another man on the head with a stick, and his tongue became heavy, he said: “The letters of the alphabet should be presented to him. For whatever of them he articulates clearly, there is nothing due in it; and whatever he cannot articulate clearly, the diyyah is due for it, and they are twenty-eight letters.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: financial compensation or blood money owed for bodily injury
key_terms.بِعَصًا: with a stick, the instrument used in the assault
key_terms.ثَمَانِيَةٌ وَ عِشْرُونَ حَرْفًا: twenty-eight letters, the total number used for calculating compensation
key_terms.حُرُوفُ الْمُعْجَمِ: the letters of the alphabet used to test speech ability
key_terms.فَثَقُلَ لِسَانُهُ: his speech became impaired or his tongue became heavy

ai.seo_question: How is blood money assessed in Shia fiqh when a head injury causes speech impairment?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for injury that impairs speech after a blow to the head. Liability is assessed by testing the injured person against the letters of the alphabet, with compensation due for the letters he can no longer pronounce properly.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5222 - Al-Bazanti narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdullah (as)

regarding a man who struck another man on the head with a stick, causing his speech to become impaired.
Imam (as) said: "He should be tested with the letters of the Arabic alphabet. For the letters he can articulate clearly, there is no liability. But for the letters he cannot pronounce clearly, there is blood money (diyyah) due for each, and the total is twenty-eight letters."
